Migrating from leaflet to glmap (For Humans & AI Agents)

Source: vignettes/leaflet-migration.Rmd
leaflet-migration.Rmd

Overview

🌱 ELI5 (3 Golden Rules to Switch from Leaflet)
Switching an existing R script or Shiny app from leaflet to glmap takes three simple habits:
  1. Replace leaflet() |> addProviderTiles(…) with glmap(basemap = “dark”) (or “positron”).
  2. Delete pal <- colorNumeric(…) and addLegend(…)—just pass color = ~column, palette = “viridis” directly into add_points() or add_polygons().
  3. In Shiny, replace leafletOutput / renderLeaflet / leafletProxy with glmapOutput / renderGlmap / glmap_proxy.

⚙️ Technical Mode (API & Reactivity Mapping)
glmap was designed so that R users and AI coding agents familiar with leaflet can transition immediately while gaining 100x–500x faster C++17 binary serialization and 60 FPS WebGL2 GPU rendering. All functions use consistent snake_case, evaluate tidy/formula aesthetics (~expr) via C/R 256-entry RGB lookup tables, and emit leaflet-compatible Shiny input events (_click, _bounds, _zoom, _marker_click, _shape_click).

Complete Function-by-Function Mapping

leaflet Function glmap Function Key Parameter Differences
leaflet(data) glmap(data, basemap = "dark") Includes basemap out of the box ("dark", "positron", "voyager", "osm", "satellite")
addTiles() / addProviderTiles() set_basemap("positron") Or set basemap = directly in glmap()
addCircleMarkers() / addMarkers() add_points() lng →\rightarrowlon, fillOpacity →\rightarrowopacity, pass color = ~col, palette = "viridis" directly
addLabelOnlyMarkers() add_labels() label →\rightarrowtext
addPolylines() add_lines() weight →\rightarrowwidth
addPolygons() add_polygons() fillColor →\rightarrowfill_color, fillOpacity →\rightarrowfill_opacity, color →\rightarrowline_color, weight →\rightarrowline_width
addRasterImage() add_raster() Streams raw Float32 values to GPU shader; supports hillshade = TRUE and live UI palette switching
addHeatmap() (leaflet.extras) add_heatmap() Built-in WebGL2 additive Gaussian kernel shader
(No built-in equivalent) add_hexbin() Built-in C++17 64-bit hexagonal spatial aggregation for 1M+ points
setView(lng, lat, zoom) set_view(lng, lat, zoom, pitch, bearing) Supports 3D camera pitch and bearing
flyTo(lng, lat, zoom) fly_to(lng, lat, zoom, pitch, bearing) Smooth WebGL camera animation
fitBounds(lng1, lat1, lng2, lat2) fit_bounds(c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)) Also accepts an sf or SpatRaster object directly
leafletOutput() / renderLeaflet() glmapOutput() / renderGlmap() Drop-in Shiny UI & Server replacements
leafletProxy() glmap_proxy() Supports clear_layer(), clear_layers(), set_layer_visibility(), set_layer_opacity(), set_raster_style(), set_filter()

Side-by-Side Migration Examples

Example 1: Polygons Colored by a Continuous Attribute

leaflet 

library(leaflet)

pal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = nc$BIR74)

leaflet(nc) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(BIR74),
    fillOpacity = 0.75,
    color = "#ffffff",
    weight = 1,
    popup = ~NAME
  ) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~BIR74, title = "Births 1974")

glmap 

library(glmap)

glmap(nc, basemap = "positron") |>
  add_polygons(
    fill_color = ~BIR74,
    palette = "viridis",
    fill_opacity = 0.75,
    line_color = "#ffffff",
    line_width = 1,
    popup = ~NAME
  )

Example 2: terra::SpatRaster with Live Interactive Shader Controls

leaflet 

# Projects and renders a static PNG in R on the CPU; changing colors requires re-running R
pal <- colorNumeric("terrain", values(dem), na.color = "transparent")
leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  addRasterImage(dem, colors = pal, opacity = 0.8)

glmap 

# Uploads raw Float32 values to GPU texture; user can switch palettes & toggle hillshade at 0ms in browser
glmap(basemap = "dark") |>
  add_raster(dem, palette = "terrain", hillshade = TRUE, opacity = 0.8)
